status: precise partial theorem independently reviewed PASS; full P12.3 unresolved

report.report:
The stated partial theorem is established in the manuscript’s precise scope. No substantive mathematical defect was found. The external statements and the chosen curve-test definition match GR25 v2; the implicit Tate-algebra facts used for the node are also supported by primary sources.

The radial classification proof covers every case. Common-denominator rational slopes can increase to the prescribed positive slopes while conductor exponents are enlarged without changing those slopes. The resulting analytic functions descend to A, and their scaled logarithms decrease because |t_i|≤1. Coordinates equal to −∞ are correctly represented by identically zero components; the all−∞ case is handled separately. For necessity, a zero branch forces nodal value at least zero by upper semicontinuity, whereas a negative branch’s radius-r disc forces a strictly negative upper bound. Shrinking discs force nodal value −∞ for every allowed nonzero profile. The Gauss-norm argument correctly identifies each disc’s singleton Shilov boundary.

The envelope calculation is complete: every admissible vector lies below h=min(φ,0), and h−1/n supplies admissible vectors converging uniformly to h. Membership of h in C_q gives exactly the stated greatest-minorant criterion. At mixed-zero h, the constructed w dominates any admissible c and strictly improves its zero-face coordinates, proving absence of maximal elements. Allowing extended profiles does not change the supremum for finite obstacles. Discreteness makes link-level upper semicontinuous regularization ineffective.

The projection contradiction uses only monotonicity, the minorant property, and fixation of C_q. The continuous-retraction obstruction also follows from density and uniqueness of limits. The displayed extensive retraction is indeed order preserving, so the manuscript correctly distinguishes these different requirements. The q=1 exception is correct.

The node satisfies the analytic hypotheses. Its equal-constant-term description gives the finite extension and conductor explicitly. Integral closedness of the disc algebras identifies B as the normalization; the two components have dimension one. Multiplicative seminorms satisfying xy=0 lie on the stated branches, with only their origins identified. The algebraic and formal normalized-link computations correctly retain the branch supports. The quotient by x^n+y has nilpotent maximal ideal, establishing the claimed m-primary principal models.

For g_n, the profiles, monotonicity, and uniform link error 1/n are correct. Its analytic supremum retains nodal value −∞, while its regularization has nodal value zero. The x-disc then has center value zero and Shilov value −1, contradicting the maximum principle. The upper-semicontinuity hypothesis of the pointwise-limit theorem is therefore unavailable. The functions are unbounded below analytically, so no bounded-product counterexample follows.

The primary-gauge factors follow directly from degree-one homogeneity, telescope, preserve signs and zero coordinates, and commute with clipping. The fixed-radius coefficients and gauge-section values are correctly distinguished. Normalization-link bijectivity does not remove the incompatible analytic values at the two origins. The final bounded nonradial example has exactly the claimed nodal and Gauss-point values, confirming that evaluation traces are less restrictive than literal radial extensions.

Harmless wording clarifications: uniqueness means uniqueness among classically psh radial extensions; the local valuation proof concerns rays with finite positive v(m), in particular the normalized link; primary gauges mean m-primary ideals. These qualifications are already supplied by the surrounding normalization scope. The undefined sentence ‘candidate is false’ should be replaced by the precise radial obstruction.

The radial classification and older nodal failure are treated as known cases, with no unsupported novelty claim. This PASS resolves only the requested partial theorem, not P12.3 or another catalogue atom. CLD comparisons, products, energy, and general geometric functoriality are not established here. The script, hashes, and repository provenance were not independently certified; they are declared supporting diagnostics and are unnecessary to the proof.

passages.statement: For complete non-Archimedean K, trivial valuation allowed, and K-analytic X, every f∈Γ(X,O_X) has classically psh log|f|, with log(0)=−∞ ([GR25, Proposition 4.2(2)](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2506.13548v2#page=21)).

For complete non-Archimedean K, trivial valuation allowed, and K-analytic X, classically psh u₁,u₂ and λ₁,λ₂≥0 give classically psh λ₁u₁+λ₂u₂ and max(u₁,u₂) ([GR25, Proposition 4.2(3)](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2506.13548v2#page=21)).

For complete non-Archimedean K, trivial valuation allowed, and K-analytic X, infima of decreasing nets of classically psh functions are classically psh ([GR25, Proposition 4.2(4)](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2506.13548v2#page=21)).

For complete non-Archimedean K, trivial valuation allowed, K-analytic f:Y→X and u:X→ℝ∪{−∞}, classically psh u implies classically psh u∘f; the converse holds for finite surjective f ([GR25, Proposition 4.2(6)](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2506.13548v2#page=21)).

For complete non-Archimedean K, trivial valuation allowed, classically psh functions on K-affinoid spaces attain their maxima at Shilov points ([GR25, Theorem 6.4](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2506.13548v2#page=33)).

For complete non-Archimedean K, trivial valuation allowed, a pointwise-convergent net of classically psh functions on K-analytic X has classically psh limit if that limit X→ℝ∪{−∞} is upper semicontinuous ([GR25, Theorem 6.5](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2506.13548v2#page=34)).

For every complete nontrivially valued non-Archimedean field K, K⟨t⟩ is a one-dimensional integrally closed domain ([Bosch, §1.2, Proposition 14](https://www.uni-muenster.de/IVV5WS/WebHop/user/weckerm/heft378.pdf#page=17); [Datta–Murayama, Theorem 2.7(ii),(iv)](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2003.13714v3#page=5)).

post_review_edits: Clarified uniqueness among radial psh extensions, normalized finite-positive valuation rays, and m-primary gauges
Replaced native candidate terminology by exact radial obstruction
Updated computational audit status; theorem and proof unchanged
reviewed_scope: For the explicitly stated disc-normalization/conductor range, the literal radial psh class has the proved clipping supremum. Mixed-zero obstacles have no maximal radial minorant and no order-preserving minorant projection fixing this class. Nodal logarithmic models and primary-gauge cocycles are explicit. The radial classification and earlier nodal failure are known cases; no general singular envelope theory is obtained.
